source_acquisition.search_note: Source inventory records no_public_source_found and the local corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-7531b7c768a9 directory is absent. The PDF, reading metadata, gh CLI searches for the full title, arXiv ID 2505.14302, OpenReview ID fXr3uPr1G5, and author repositories, plus unicli scholar code/sources queries, yielded no repository directly containing this paper’s Figure 1–16 or Table 1–4 sources. ChenMnZ/INT_vs_FP is a separate ICML paper; PrefixQuant, EfficientQAT, and OmniQuant only cite or mention the work; voidful/icml2026 is conference metadata; the quantization exercise repository is unrelated. Therefore all visual evidence is from the verified PDF and 200 dpi rendered observation.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Categorical tab10 colors and marker shapes are reused for model-size/group-size series; magma-like sequential contours encode scalar error, ratio, and EPM surfaces; Figure 15 uses semantic pastel module fills. No single colorblind-safe or grayscale-safe standard is enforced.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The PDF figures, contours, diagrams, table rules, and text are predominantly vector objects; no target visual-source files were found, and pdfimages identifies only unrelated page-1 raster resources.
paper_style.style_consistency: The SFRM/Computer Modern math caption and table system is stable, and DejaVu Sans/ByteSans plot labels recur; predicted–actual and N/D/G grammars are intentionally reused. Local inconsistencies remain in baseline colors, small legends, hidden fit metrics, Figure 4(c) model labeling, Table 1 γG, and the truncated Figure 16 caption.

figures.label: Figure 1 (a,b)

caption.text: Figure 1 Quantization error contour based on the proposed unified QAT scaling law. The quantization error decreases as the model size increases, but increases with both the number of training tokens and with coarser quantization granularity.

color.semantic_mapping: Sequential contour levels encode quantization-error magnitude; direct numeric contour labels provide the level key, with panel facets for W4A4G32 and W4A4G256.

encodings.x: Model Size N on a log axis
encodings.y: Training Tokens D on a log axis
encodings.text: Direct error labels and panel labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Analytic contour rendering from the proposed unified QAT law, with log-scaled N and D domains and approximately eight labeled error levels per panel. The PDF gives no raw grid, sample count, fitted range, or uncertainty display.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction claim that quantization error falls with N but rises with D and coarse G → Figure 1 visualizes two fixed-G slices → Appendix G derives the log-space contour from Eq. (5).
design_strengths: Fixed-G small multiples turn a three-variable law into a readable geometric comparison.
Direct labels remove a separate legend and preserve the direction of the contours.
Log axes match the multiplicative scaling-law form.
design_weaknesses: Sequential color levels are hard to distinguish in grayscale or for adjacent values.
The caption does not state the G values; that mapping is left to panel labels.
No observations, fit domain, or uncertainty are shown, so the contour is a model interface rather than an empirical residual diagnostic.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a plug-in scaling function, show fixed-variable log contours first, then connect them to observed slices and fit diagnostics.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2 Integer (INT4) vs. floating-point (FP4) in W4A4, 297M model, 50B tokens.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue circles/solid line denote INT4, orange squares/solid line denote FP4, and the green dashed horizontal line is the uncompressed baseline.

encodings.shape: Circle for INT4 and square for FP4
encodings.line: Solid format series versus dashed baseline

figures.data_and_statistics: Point estimates of loss at five group granularities for a 297M model trained on 50B tokens; the panel compares INT4, FP4, and an uncompressed baseline. No replicate spread, error bar, or sample denominator is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: Training-setup format choice → Figure 2 compares INT4/FP4 over group size → Figure 13 tests transfer of an INT4-fitted law to FP4.
design_strengths: Color, marker, and line style jointly distinguish the three roles.
Fixing model size and token count isolates the group-size comparison.
The horizontal baseline gives an immediate loss anchor.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define the baseline precision or loss construction.
Long categorical ticks consume the narrow panel width.
No repeated runs or uncertainty make small format gaps difficult to assess.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a format sweep with a horizontal uncompressed anchor when selecting a quantization representation.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3 δW4A4 at different learning rates, W4A4 (G = 128) 145M model, 20B tokens.

color.semantic_mapping: A single blue circle/line series encodes δW4A4 over the learning-rate sweep.

figures.data_and_statistics: Five point estimates of δW4A4 for a 145M W4A4 model at G=128 and 20B tokens. The plot has no baseline, replicate information, or uncertainty; the body text describes an approximately constant range but the rendered y-axis is around 0.055–0.075.
figures.evidence_relation: Training-hyperparameter sensitivity claim → Figure 3 checks learning-rate dependence → the paper reuses common BF16/QAT hyperparameters in later scaling experiments.
design_strengths: Minimal single-series grammar keeps the sweep legible.
The full categorical learning-rate set is visible without interpolation.
The fixed G, N, and D settings are placed in the caption.
design_weaknesses: Without a BF16 reference or spread, stability is judged from only five points.
δW4A4 is not defined in the caption.
The body text range [0.6, 0.65] appears inconsistent in scale with the plotted y-axis, a potential reporting error.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a single outcome series for a hyperparameter sensitivity check, while reporting a reference and uncertainty when stability matters.

figures.label: Figure 4 (a–c)

(c) δW4A4 decreases with smaller group sizes. Note that these trends of δW4A4 are consistent across different N, D, and G. For simplicity, we merely plot the model trained with 100B tokens in (a), a model size of 594M in (b), and the 594M model trained with 100B tokens in (c).

color.semantic_mapping: Five tab10 colors and five marker shapes identify Group32, Group64, Group128, Group256, and Token/Channel series across N, D, and G slices.

encodings.shape: Marker shape repeats the group-size identity

encodings.text: Panel subtitles, legend, and 0.037 gap arrow

figures.evidence_relation: Unified-law observation and Eq. (5) → Figure 4 establishes N/D/G directions → Table 1 fits exponents and Figure 5 validates the combined law.
design_strengths: The same color/marker grammar is reused across all three resource axes.
Small multiples separate N, D, and G while preserving a common y outcome.
The caption states the fixed-variable slices and the main directional findings.
design_weaknesses: Five curves overlap in narrow panels and the legend appears only once.
Panel (c) says Model=567M inside the plot while the caption/body say 594M.
Representative slices omit variability and do not establish the full three-dimensional surface alone.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a common series grammar for N/D/G slices, explicitly state the fixed values, and reserve a later multivariate fit for interpolation.

caption.text: Figure 5 Fitting performance of δW4A4 scaling laws.

color.semantic_mapping: Model-size categories use blue/orange/green/red points; yellow star marks the 973M validation set.

Model-size categories primarily depend on color, which weakens in grayscale.
Generic MSE/R² in the plot title summarize fit but do not expose heterogeneity over N/D/G.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a fixed predicted–actual canvas, identity reference, and an explicit validation marker for scaling-law fit checks.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6 Quantization error decomposition. δW4A4 = k(δW16A4 + δW4A16).

color.semantic_mapping: Five tab10 series encode group-size conditions; marker shape and color identify G, while the black dashed line encodes the fitted 0.906 slope.

figures.evidence_relation: Decomposition hypothesis → Figure 6 tests the additive component relation → Figure 7 expands each component over N/D/G and Figure 8 forms their ratio.
design_strengths: The slope reference turns the decomposition into a geometric test.
Color and marker redundancy make group-size deviations inspectable.
The axes directly match the proposed equation.
design_weaknesses: The caption leaves k undefined and does not state that 0.906 is an observed coefficient.
Five series crowd the same scatter canvas.
No fit uncertainty or residual diagnostics are visible.
figures.reusable_pattern: Plot a total against component sum with an explicitly labeled fitted slope when a decomposition is the mechanism claim.

Gap arrows foreground the different G sensitivity.

The gap arrows are not explained in the total caption.

Vertical percentage arrows attach relative improvements to each G.

The percentage arrows are not defined in the caption, including their denominator.
Kurtosis and loss are point summaries with no distribution or seed variability.

figures.label: Figure 13

caption.text: Figure 13 The QAT scaling law, fitted for INT4 quantization, also accurately models the quantization error of FP4 quantization.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/orange colors identify the 145M and 298M model-size groups; the black dashed identity line is a separate reference.

encodings.y: Predicted FP4 δW4A4 error from INT4 fit

figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2 establishes INT4/FP4 comparability → Figure 13 tests INT4-fit transfer to FP4 → conclusion claims similar scaling behavior.
design_strengths: The unchanged identity-line grammar makes format transfer easy to inspect.
The caption clearly states fit format versus target format.
A compact two-category plot avoids unnecessary facet proliferation.
design_weaknesses: Only two model sizes are shown and both rely on color.
There is no separate marker for fit/target format or validation status.
Metrics and sampling details are confined to the plot title/body.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a cross-format transfer test, keep the predicted–actual canvas fixed and state the fit/target direction explicitly.

figures.label: Figure 14 (a,b)

caption.text: (a) Weight quantizer ablation. (b) Activation quantizer ablation. Figure 14 Quantizer ablation studies for 145M model with 50B tokens.

color.semantic_mapping: Weight-panel LSQ/LWC/AbsMax and red baseline, and activation-panel LAC/AbsMax and green baseline use separate series colors; baseline color changes between panels.

encodings.line: Solid quantizer lines and dashed baseline

figures.evidence_relation: Training setup selects AbsMax/LAC → Figure 14 tests weight and activation quantizer choices → Appendix I explains the per-tensor activation failure via outliers.
design_strengths: Separating weight and activation choices prevents a seven-series overlay.
The baseline line anchors the ablation outcome in each panel.
The sharp per-tensor activation rise exposes the outlier-sensitive failure mode.

Baseline color changes from red to green, breaking a stable semantic cue.
Caption does not define channel/token/tensor granularity or the marker mapping.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1 Fitted hyperparameters and their values in our proposed QAT error scaling law.

tables.uncertainty: None shown; all entries are fitted constants, deterministic comparisons, or point percentages. No standard errors, intervals, seeds, replicates, or uncertainty columns are displayed.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six visible columns form two symmetric Type | Constant | Value blocks. Body groups are Chinchilla (E, A, α, B, β), δW4A16, δW4A4 with FC2 input 8-bit, δW4A4, δW16A4, and δW16A4 with FC2 input 8-bit; values are mostly reported to four decimal places.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 4/7 trends and Figure 5/6 fits → Table 1 fixes the constants/exponents used by Eq. (5) and its component variants.
design_strengths: Symmetric blocks put several precision variants on one comparable surface.
Four-decimal values are convenient for reproduction.
Minimal horizontal rules preserve a clean math-table hierarchy.
design_weaknesses: Merged labels and blank alignment rows increase scan cost.
No fit error or parameter uncertainty is included.
The δW16A4 FC2-input-8-bit γG is 0.4491 in the table while body text reports 0.4471.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use symmetric Type/Constant/Value blocks for several variants of one equation, while documenting shared units and fit uncertainty.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2 Comparison with other scaling laws. “Num” indicates the number of scaling laws fitted. “Relative Error” represents the difference between the predicted and actual quantization errors.

tables.uncertainty: None shown; all entries are fitted constants, deterministic comparisons, or point percentages. No standard errors, intervals, seeds, replicates, or uncertainty columns are displayed.
tables.data_and_statistics: Eight columns record Method, N, D, G, δp, Precision, Num. of δp, and Relative Error. Prior and Ours are two row groups with two precision rows each; ✓/× encode variable inclusion, Num is 5 versus 1, and Ours relative errors 5.2% and 4.7% are bold.
tables.evidence_relation: Eq. (3) variable omission versus Eq. (5) unified coverage → Table 2 closes the main-text comparison with fit count and relative-error outcomes.
design_strengths: The variable-coverage, fit-complexity, and error dimensions form a compact decision surface.
Bold is reserved for the two proposed relative-error values.
The table note defines Num and Relative Error.
design_weaknesses: Multirow precision entries require vertical scanning across dashed separators.
“Difference” is not given as a formula or aggregation rule.
The ✓/× variable semantics are not expanded in the caption and no uncertainty is shown.
tables.reusable_pattern: Compare a law extension using one table that exposes variable coverage, number of fitted curves, and resulting error.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3 Model architecture and training hyper-parameters.

tables.uncertainty: None shown; all entries are fitted constants, deterministic comparisons, or point percentages. No standard errors, intervals, seeds, replicates, or uncertainty columns are displayed.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 gives N/D/G contour intuition; Figures 2–3 remove format and learning-rate confounders; Figures 4–6 establish slices, unified fit, and additive components; Figures 7–9 expand component sensitivity into ratio, FC2 outlier, and 8-bit intervention evidence; Table 2 closes the main comparison. Appendix Figures 10–16 and Tables 3–4 provide baseline, precision transfer, quantizer, architecture, EPM, and D-term checks.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use a consistent Figure/Table number plus sentence-case English description, with bold ByteSans object labels. Composite trend figures often put panel findings in separate headers; fit metrics are placed in plot titles rather than captions. Captions rarely state sample counts or uncertainty, and Figure 16 is physically truncated.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The four tables use distinct but coherent decision layouts: symmetric Type/Constant/Value blocks, variable-coverage comparison, model-size columns, and precision-by-ablation. All use minimal/booktabs-like horizontal rules without vertical grids or uncertainty columns.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 and Figure 15 provide law/interface and architecture anchors; Figures 2–4 establish experimental choices and directional trends; Figures 5–8 fit and decompose the law; Figure 9, Figure 14, and Table 4 localize and ablate bottlenecks; Figure 16 translates the law into an efficiency decision surface.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The body points to Appendix C for Chinchilla fitting, Appendix E for quantizer and precision-transfer details, Appendix F for architecture/settings, Appendix G for contour derivation, and Appendix H/I for EPM and D-term analysis. The appendix objects extend rather than replace the Figure 1–9 evidence chain.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: SFRM/Computer Modern math carries captions, equations, and tables; DejaVu Sans carries plot axes and legends; ByteSans-Bold emphasizes Figure/Table labels. Small plot text is approximately 6–10 pt, while the architecture diagram uses heavier sans-serif box labels.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Tab10 categorical colors and markers recur across Figures 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11–14; magma-like sequential contours are reserved for Figures 1, 8, and 16; Figure 9 uses hatch and Figure 15 uses semantic fills. Baseline color changes in Figure 14 and the absence of a global grayscale/colorblind rule are consistency weaknesses.

most_reusable_patterns: Fixed predicted–actual canvases with an identity reference for scaling-law fit and transfer checks.
N/D/G small multiples with shared series grammar, then component rows for direct sensitivity comparison.
Log-domain ratio/EPM contours with a few interpretable D:N slices for mechanism-to-decision evidence.
A mechanism diagnostic next to its targeted intervention outcome, with local gain annotations.
Compact tables that expose variable coverage, fitted-curve complexity, and relative error together.
highest_value_objects: Figure 5: Eq. (5) W4A4 fit and 973M validation.
Figures 6–9: decomposition, ratio, FC2 bottleneck, and 8-bit intervention chain.
Table 2: prior versus proposed law in one decision surface.
Figure 16: scaling law translated into an EPM decision contour.
failure_patterns: Captions usually omit sample size, replicate structure, uncertainty, and metric definitions.
Model-size scatter series rely heavily on color and hide fit metrics in plot titles.
Figure 4(c) shows Model=567M while the caption/body state 594M.
Table 1 γG for δW16A4 with FC2 input is 0.4491 while body text gives 0.4471.
Figure 16 has a truncated caption and apparent W4W4 typo, with no contour color key.
Figure 14 changes baseline color between panels.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use a consistent log-contour and predicted–actual grammar to turn the N/D/G QAT law into a visible prediction, then use component small multiples, FC2 intervention panels, and compact ablations to reach precision-allocation and EPM decisions.
